title: Agoda AI Developer Report 2026
sample_note: sample not disclosed
geography: Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam, India
headline_stat: 53% of developers use AI agents in selected production workflows or broadly across their organizations
note: Conducted with Macramé Consulting; read from the release as published by Hotel News Resource. Only 38% say their codebase is mostly or fully ready for autonomous agents.

title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q3 2026
sample_note: 314 US C-suite and business leaders
headline_stat: 62% of organizations are building, deploying or developing AI agents, up from 53%; 25% are actively developing or implementing multi-agent systems
note: The measure widened this quarter from deployment to building, deploying or developing, so 62% is not directly comparable with the earlier deployment figures.

title: The Impact of Agentic AI on Network Operations
sample_note: 1,000 IT and network operations leaders at organizations with 500 or more employees
headline_stat: 51% run agentic AI that acts in production network operations today; 75% have deployed AI for network operations
note: Conducted independently by Omdia for Cisco. Covers network operations only, not agents across the business.

title: The state of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
sample_note: 1,719 participants in 97 nations across regions, industries, company sizes, functions and tenures; 36% work for organizations with more than $1 billion in annual revenue
headline_stat: 40% of respondents from organizations with more than $1 billion in revenue report scaling AI agents in one or more functions (up from 27%); 22% of respondents from smaller organizations
note: The 40% is the large-organization subgroup (more than $1 billion revenue), not all respondents; McKinsey gives 22% for smaller organizations and no all-respondent agent share on the page. Responses are weighted by each nation's share of global GDP. The page gives no definition of an AI agent.

title: The State of Development 2026
sample_note: 554 engineers and engineering leaders who currently use AI agents
agent_definition: "An LLM instance capable of taking multi-step actions on its own."
headline_stat: 80.8% of engineers who use AI agents use them daily, up from 47.3% a year earlier
note: Respondents had to be using AI agents to qualify (Qualtrics panel), so the figure is frequency of use among users, not adoption.

title: Annual survey of enterprise data leaders (interim findings)
sample_note: more than 540 enterprise data leaders and practitioners in 66 countries
headline_stat: 23.5% already use AI agents in production in data and analytics workflows; 33.8% are piloting
note: Interim findings, read via IT Brief. Covers data and analytics workflows only. The sponsor sells a data platform marketed for AI agents.

title: AI agents are only the beginning: The path to agentic transformation
sample_note: 501 US senior managers to C-suite at organizations at least piloting agentic AI
headline_stat: 43% are expanding AI agent deployments across functions and 15% have reached scaled, orchestrated multi-agent adoption; 42% are still testing
note: 58% adds the two stages beyond testing (43% plus 15%). Every organization had to be at least piloting agentic AI to take part, so this is not a population adoption rate.

title: VB Pulse: Where enterprise AI agent governance hasn't caught up
sample_note: 573 qualified respondents across five parallel surveys, organizations with 100 or more employees
agent_definition: true agents: deployed agents that "can complete multi-step work on their own"
headline_stat: 71% say a quarter or fewer of their deployed "agents" can complete multi-step work on their own; only 10% say true agents are the majority of what they run
note: Self-selected, not a probability sample, as VentureBeat states. Measures how many deployed agents are real agents, not adoption.

title: Booz Allen survey of federal agencies on agentic AI
sample_note: 105 federal government IT and cybersecurity decision-makers and influencers
headline_stat: Only 7% of federal agencies have agentic AI in production; 51% are piloting or testing and 22% plan to deploy within 12 months
note: Fielded online with Market Connections. Read via GovInfoSecurity's report of the release; the any-use figure (58%) adds piloting and production.

title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q2 2026
sample_note: 204 US C-suite and business leaders
headline_stat: 53% agent deployment, on par with the prior quarter
note: This release gives the prior quarter as 55%; the Q1 2026 release itself said 54%.

title: 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise
series: Box State of AI in the Enterprise
sample_note: 1,640 IT decision-makers in the US, UK, France and Japan
geography: United States, United Kingdom, France, Japan
headline_stat: 83% of organizations are running AI agents; 19% run them autonomously at scale
note: Respondents self-selected into four AI-maturity tiers. Box sells AI agents for enterprise content.

title: AI at Work 2026
sample_note: 11,749 workers in 14 markets
headline_stat: 30% of respondents say AI agents are already integrated into their workflows, more than double the 13% a year earlier
note: 52% of respondents say they have a limited understanding of what agents are.

title: 2026 State of AI Development
sample_note: nearly 1,900 IT leaders worldwide, including 527 in Asia Pacific
headline_stat: 96% of organizations are already using AI agents in some capacity; 94% worry about AI sprawl
note: Fielded by an unnamed third party. "In some capacity" is the loosest use measure in the index.

title: Enterprise AI adoption in 2026
sample_note: 1,200 C-suite executives and 1,200 non-technical employees who use AI at work
headline_stat: 97% of executives say their company deployed AI agents in the past year; 52% of employees already use them
note: Fielded with Workplace Intelligence. The highest deployment figure in the index; the same survey finds only 23% see significant ROI from agents.

title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q1 2026
sample_note: 237 US C-suite and business leaders
headline_stat: 54% of organizations are actively deploying AI agents; 63% now require human validation of agent outputs
note: Organizations with $1 billion or more in annual revenue; more than a third above $10 billion.

title: The State of AI in the Enterprise, 2026
series: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise
sample_note: 3,235 senior business and IT leaders directly involved in AI programs
headline_stat: 23% of companies use agentic AI at least moderately today; 74% expect to within two years; 21% have mature agent governance
note: The report prints its question wording ("To what extent is your organization utilizing agentic AI in its operations?").

title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q4 2025
sample_note: 130 US C-suite and business leaders
headline_stat: 26% of organizations report agent deployment, down from 42% in Q3; KPMG attributes part of the drop to leaders adopting stricter definitions of a true agent
note: The release says leaders "adopt more sophisticated definitions of what constitutes a true agent", the clearest case in this index of a definition moving a headline number.

title: G2 AI agents survey (August 2025), cited in G2's Enterprise AI Agents Report
sample_note: sample not disclosed
headline_stat: 57% of companies already have AI agents in production; 22% are piloting
note: G2 cites its own August 2025 survey without sample or respondent details on the page read.

title: 2025: The State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
series: Menlo State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
sample_note: 495 US enterprise AI decision-makers
agent_definition: "systems where an LLM plans and executes actions, observes feedback, and adapts its behavior"
headline_stat: Only 16% of enterprise and 27% of startup AI deployments qualify as true agents
note: A share of deployments, not of organizations, so it sits outside the adoption ranges. The strictest definition in the index and one of the lowest numbers. Menlo invests in AI companies.

title: State of Agent Engineering
sample_note: 1,340 responses to a public survey
headline_stat: 57.3% of respondents have agents in production; another 30.4% are developing agents with concrete plans to deploy
note: Open, self-selected survey of a framework vendor's audience; 49% of respondents work at companies under 100 people. The prior edition reported 51%.

publisher: MIT Sloan Management Review and BCG
title: The Emerging Agentic Enterprise: How Leaders Must Navigate a New Age of AI
series: MIT SMR-BCG AI and Business Strategy
sample_note: sample not disclosed on the report page read
sponsor: MIT Sloan Management Review and Boston Consulting Group
headline_stat: 35% of organizations have adopted agentic AI within two years; another 44% plan to deploy it soon
note: Global executive survey; the web report describes agentic AI as systems that "can plan, act, and learn on their own" but the page read gives no sample size.

title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
sample_note: 1,993 participants in 105 nations, all regions, industries and company sizes
agent_definition: "systems based on foundation models capable of acting in the real world, planning and executing multiple steps in a workflow"
headline_stat: 23% are scaling an agentic AI system somewhere in the enterprise; 62% are at least experimenting with AI agents
note: Responses weighted by each nation's contribution to global GDP. McKinsey has since replaced this page with its 2026 edition; the 2025 figures were read from the Internet Archive capture of 2 January 2026.

title: Gartner Survey Finds Just 15% of IT Application Leaders Are Considering, Piloting, or Deploying Fully Autonomous AI Agents
sample_note: 360 IT application leaders at organizations with 250 or more employees
agent_definition: fully autonomous AI agents: "goal driven AI tools that do not require human oversight"
headline_stat: 15% of IT application leaders are considering, piloting or deploying fully autonomous AI agents
note: Counts only fully autonomous agents, a far stricter bar than most surveys, so it sits outside the adoption ranges. It shows what happens to the number when "agent" means no human in the loop.

title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q3 2025
sample_note: 130 US C-suite and business leaders
headline_stat: 42% of organizations have deployed at least some AI agents, up from 11% two quarters earlier
note: Organizations with $1 billion or more in annual revenue.

title: The ROI of AI 2025
sample_note: sample not disclosed on the page read (the full report is gated)
geography: Not stated on the page read
headline_stat: 52% of executives report their organizations are deploying AI agents in production; 39% have deployed more than 10 agents
note: The public summary gives no sample size or dates; method details sit behind a form.

title: Rise of agentic AI: How trust is the key to human-AI collaboration
sample_note: 1,500 executives (director level and above) at organizations with over $1 billion in revenue
agent_definition: "programs/platforms/software that are connected to the business environment with a defined boundary, make decisions autonomously, and act to achieve specific goals with or without human intervention"
headline_stat: 14% have deployed AI agents (2% at scale, 12% at partial scale); 23% have launched pilots and 61% are exploring
note: Every respondent organization had already started exploring agentic AI, so the sample is screened toward interest. The any-use figure (37%) adds deployed and piloting. Capgemini reconfirmed 900 of 1,500 responses.

title: 2025 Stack Overflow Developer Survey: AI
sample_note: 31,877 answered the AI agents question (49,009 survey responses from 177 countries)
agent_definition: "autonomous software entities that can operate with minimal to no direct human intervention using artificial intelligence techniques"
headline_stat: 30.9% of developers use AI agents at work (14.1% daily, 9% weekly, 7.8% monthly or less); 37.9% do not and do not plan to
note: The 30.9% sums the three published yes answers. Respondents were recruited mainly through Stack Overflow's own channels.

title: AI at Work 2025: Momentum Builds, but Gaps Remain
sample_note: more than 10,600 leaders, managers and frontline employees in 11 countries and regions
agent_definition: "smart digital assistants capable of learning, reasoning, and handling complex tasks independently"
headline_stat: 13% of employees see AI agents deeply integrated into their daily workflows
note: Only one third of employees said they understand how agents work.

title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q2 2025
sample_note: 130 US C-suite and business leaders
headline_stat: 33% of organizations have deployed at least some AI agents, up threefold after two quarters at 11%
note: Organizations with $1 billion or more in annual revenue.

title: Gartner poll of webinar attendees on agentic AI investment (in the June 2025 agentic AI cancellation forecast)
sample_note: 3,412 webinar attendees
headline_stat: 19% say their organization has made significant investments in agentic AI and 42% conservative ones; 31% are waiting or unsure
note: Measures investment, not use, so it sits outside the adoption ranges. Webinar attendees are a self-selected, interested audience. The same release estimates only about 130 of thousands of agentic AI vendors are real.

title: PwC's AI Agent Survey
sample_note: 308 US business executives (33% C-suite, 13% VP, 54% director)
headline_stat: 79% of executives say AI agents are already being adopted in their companies; of adopters, 66% report measurable productivity value
note: "Adopted" is not defined; PwC itself notes that reports of full adoption often reflect excitement rather than evidence of transformation, and 68% say half or fewer of their employees interact with agents.

title: EY Technology Pulse Poll: technology companies set the pace of agentic AI
sample_note: 504 US business leaders in the technology industry at organizations with 5,000 or more employees
headline_stat: 48% of technology leaders are already adopting or fully deploying agentic AI
note: Fielded online by Atomik Research; margin of error plus or minus 4 points. Technology companies only.

title: 2025 Work Trend Index: The year the Frontier Firm is born
sample_note: 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets, including 9,037 leaders
headline_stat: 46% of leaders say their companies are using agents to fully automate workflows or processes
note: Fielded by Edelman Data x Intelligence; the report prints the survey question under each chart.

title: The Future of Enterprise AI Agents
sample_note: nearly 1,500 enterprise IT leaders in 14 countries
headline_stat: 57% of enterprise IT leaders say they implemented AI agents in the past two years; 96% plan to expand their use
note: Sample size given as approximately 1,500.

title: KPMG AI Quarterly Pulse Survey, Q1 2025
sample_note: 130 US C-suite and business leaders
headline_stat: 11% of organizations are deploying AI agents (flat on the prior quarter); 65% are piloting them, up from 37%
note: Organizations with $1 billion or more in annual revenue.

title: AI agents in 2025: Expectations vs. reality (IBM and Morning Consult developer survey)
sample_note: 1,000 developers building AI applications for enterprise
headline_stat: 99% of developers building enterprise AI applications say they are exploring or developing AI agents
note: Reported in a quote on IBM's own page; "exploring" sets a very low bar, and the sample is developers already building AI applications.
